findings.title: Cleanup interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The background cleanup loop now runs all cleanup jobs every minute instead of every 10 minutes. This is a global behavior change that affects more than annotation cleanup and can substantially increase DB and filesystem load; it looks accidental or at least undocumented.

findings.title: Error-level logging of every cleanup batch and full ID list
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags log at Error level for every successful batch, include the full IDs slice, and log err=nil. With small batch sizes, large backlogs, or the 1-minute cleanup ticker, this can flood logs, create very long log lines, and trigger error-based alerts. These should be Debug/Trace and should not log full ID lists.

findings.title: Batch loop may stop early if selected rows are deleted concurrently
findings.body: The fetch-then-delete implementation treats a DELETE that affects zero rows as completion. If another process deletes all IDs selected in a batch between fetchIDs and deleteByIDs, affected will be 0 even though more eligible rows remain, so cleanup stops for this cycle. Consider looping until fetchIDs returns no IDs.

findings.title: SQLite IN list is built with O(n^2) string concatenation
findings.body: When avoiding SQLite parameter limits, the code builds the IN clause by repeatedly calling fmt.Sprintf with the previous string. For large batch sizes this causes quadratic allocations/copying and can slow cleanup; a strings.Builder or joined list would be safer.
